result:
There is a particular kind of quiet that arrives after the rain stops, before anyone has noticed it has stopped. Water slips from the leaves one drop at a time. A car passes, sounding farther away than it is. Somewhere, a bird tests a single note and waits.

Nothing important has happened. The street is the same street, the afternoon the same afternoon. But for a minute, the world seems to be listening to itself.

I like that minute. It asks nothing of me—not to improve, decide, or make good use of the time. It lets me stand at the window and watch a drop gather at the tip of a branch until it is too heavy to stay.
